title: Photochromic Lens Reaction Lab
description: Users operate a UV lamp (barn lamp) to trigger a simulated photochromic chemical reaction on spectacle lenses (sunglasses). By adjusting UV wavelength, intensity, and exposure duration, users control the reversible darkening reaction of silver chloride molecules embedded in the lens, observing real-time tint changes and reaction kinetics on a heads-up display.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a photochromic lens chemistry lab. Load SunglassesKhronos.glb centered at (0,1,0) and AnisotropyBarnLamp.glb positioned at (-2,2,1) angled toward the sunglasses. The barn lamp represents a tunable UV light source used to drive a photochromic reaction (AgCl → Ag + Cl) in the sunglasses lenses.

Camera: perspective camera at (0,2,4) looking at the sunglasses, with OrbitControls limited to a 120-degree arc.

Lighting: ambient light at 0.3 intensity, plus a SpotLight parented to the barn lamp model that visually represents the UV beam hitting the lenses. The spotlight cone should visibly illuminate the glasses.

Interaction steps (6-10 with validation):
1. Click the barn lamp to power it ON — lamp emissive material glows, spotlight activates.
2. Use a wavelength slider (280-400nm) — validate range, update spotlight color from deep violet to near-invisible UV. Display wavelength on an HTML overlay panel.
3. Use an intensity slider (0-100%) — validate 0-100, scale spotlight intensity and beam width accordingly.
4. Click an 'Expose' button to start a 5-second exposure timer shown as a progress bar.
5. During exposure, the sunglasses lens material must animate: gradually change opacity and color from clear (transparent) to dark brown/gray, simulating silver nanoparticle formation. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial transmission and color properties.
6. After exposure, display a reaction kinetics panel showing calculated reaction rate based on wavelength and intensity (rate = intensity * (1/(wavelength-270))). Validate the rate is positive.
7. Click a 'Reverse Reaction' button to animate lenses back to clear over 3 seconds, simulating thermal reversal.
8. A 'Log Result' button stores the trial parameters into a visible table (up to 5 entries). Validate no duplicate wavelength+intensity combos.

Add an HTML overlay panel styled semi-transparent dark with white text for all controls and data display. All parameter inputs must show validation error messages for out-of-range values. Include a subtle particle effect between lamp and glasses during exposure to represent photon flux.
